role: The overworld surface pass: ChunkProviderGenerate.func_147422_a over one chunk and each biome's func_150573_a (the generic top/filler/bedrock column, Mesa bands and Bryce spires, hills, mega taiga, Savanna M, mutated dispatch), writing block ids and metas into the chunk arrays.

structs.name: struct surface
structs.java: state the biome objects keep: each BiomeGenBase.topBlock, and BiomeGenMesa's field_150621_aC, field_150625_aG, field_150623_aE, field_150624_aF

gpu: line 258, function column: recursion for SURF_MUTATED into the base biome (depth 1 in practice, a mutated biome's base is not mutated)
line 270, 289, 302, function column: writes the per-biome topBlock back into struct surface (mutable per-world state carried across columns, mirroring Java's biome singletons)
line 159, function mesa_column: libm cos, whose sign only is used (the note says StrictMath.cos in Java)
notes: Called from chunkgen.c when a chunk is generated, which happens inside the server tick as chunks load. The swamp override places nothing in 1.7.10 (its loop exits on air at y 255), so SURF_SWAMP falls through to the generic column. Mesa's spire noises come from Random(0) in a fresh JVM, a quirk the port keeps. The Java member names were matched by grep against ChunkProviderGenerate.java and BiomeGenMesa.java; the hills, taiga and savanna field names are taken from the port's comments. surface_tops_merge sets the topBlock entries a pass over a chunk's biomes wrote from that pass's table (the provider state a generation run elsewhere leaves, lane/gpugen).
